name: Fluconazole
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Fluconazole is cleared mainly by the kidneys as unchanged drug. The US label gives a usual loading dose, then 50% of the daily dose at creatinine clearance (CrCl) 50 mL/min or below, and 100% of the dose after each hemodialysis (a 3-hour session lowers levels by about 50%). Single-dose 150 mg for vaginal candidiasis needs no change.

bands.recommendation: CrCl >50: usual dose (100%) (label). Single 150 mg dose for vaginal candidiasis: no change at any kidney function.
CrCl 51–59: usual dose. CrCl ≤50: Give the usual loading dose (50 to 400 mg), then 50% of the usual daily dose (label: CrCl ≤50 without dialysis).
Give the usual loading dose (50 to 400 mg), then 50% of the usual daily dose (label: CrCl ≤50 without dialysis).
Give the usual loading dose (50 to 400 mg), then 50% of the usual daily dose (label: CrCl ≤50 without dialysis).

hd.text: 100% of the recommended dose after each hemodialysis; on non-dialysis days a reduced dose by CrCl (label). A 3-hour session lowers plasma levels by about 50%.

pd.text: No PD dosing in label. For PD-associated fungal peritonitis (ISPD 2022): oral route preferred, 200 mg loading dose then 100 mg daily (Table 6); intraperitoneal 150–200 mg every 24 to 48 hours (Table 5). Specialist input.

crrt.text: Li 2020 (CRRT review, Table 3): CVVH ultrafiltration 1 L/h, 400 mg every 24 h; ultrafiltration 2.4–3.2 L/h, load 12 mg/kg lean body weight then 6 mg/kg every 24 h. CVVHD dialysate 1 L/h, 800 mg every 24 h; dialysate 4 L/h, load 900 mg then 600 mg every 12 h. CVVHDF (ultrafiltration 2 L/h plus dialysate 1 L/h), 400 mg every 12 h. Dose rises with effluent rate.

dialyzable: Yes: a 3-hour hemodialysis session lowers plasma levels by about 50% (label). Protein binding 11% to 12%.
monitoring: Kidney function for dose; liver tests; QT interval with other QT-prolonging drugs; potassium and magnesium. Levels of interacting drugs (tacrolimus, cyclosporine, warfarin, phenytoin, sulfonylureas).

pediatric.approved_ages: 6 months and older for oropharyngeal and esophageal candidiasis and cryptococcal meningitis; systemic Candida dosing from birth (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Oropharyngeal or esophageal candidiasis: 6 mg/kg day 1, then 3 mg/kg daily (up to 12 mg/kg/day for esophageal). Systemic Candida, 3 months and older: 25 mg/kg day 1 (maximum 800 mg), then 12 mg/kg daily (maximum 400 mg). Cryptococcal meningitis: 12 mg/kg day 1, then 6 to 12 mg/kg daily (label).
pediatric.max_dose: 12 mg/kg/day; systemic Candida maximum 800 mg loading and 400 mg daily.
pediatric.neonates: Birth to 3 months, gestational age 30 weeks or more: 25 mg/kg day 1, then 12 mg/kg daily; under 30 weeks: 25 mg/kg day 1, then 9 mg/kg daily (systemic Candida; label Table 6).
pediatric.notes: Label pediatric CrCl formula: K × height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL); K = 0.55 for children over 1 year, 0.45 for infants.

renal.recommendation: Label: not studied in children with kidney impairment, but dose reduction should parallel adults (50% of daily dose if CrCl ≤50, after the loading dose), CrCl by height-based formula (label).
Parallel adult rule: loading dose, then 50% of daily dose (label).
Parallel adult rule: loading dose, then 50% of daily dose (label).

hd.text: Parallel adult rule: full dose after each hemodialysis (label says pediatric reduction should parallel adults; not studied).

crrt.text: No pediatric CRRT data in the cited sources. Specialist input.
